bullets.title: NVDA: $105B OpenAI Ohio data center backstop; secures 35-40% of global HBM supply; UBS estimates $1B/day FCF
bullets.body: NVIDIA agreed to back up to $105B of OpenAI's 20-year Ohio data center lease (8GW capacity, first 800MW online 2028), which could generate ~$600B in revenue by 2030. Separately, NVDA has secured 35-40% of global HBM supply for 2027 and Ark Invest bought 97,970 shares Monday. UBS estimates NVDA will reach $1B/day in FCF with consensus revenue ranging $630-700B+. LG Electronics is also deepening robotics collaboration with NVDA.

bullets.title: FN: Beat and raise on optical acceleration; Wolfe upgrades to Outperform, $775 PT; JPM raises PT to $695
bullets.body: Fabrinet Q4 FY26 revenue $1.316B (beat $1.276B est.) and EPS $4.10 (beat $3.81 est.); Q1 guidance $1.375-1.425B vs. $1.334B consensus and EPS $4.10-4.25 vs. $4.00. Wolfe upgrades to Outperform ($775 PT, 29.5% upside) citing new transceiver wins and capacity ramp to $12.5-14B annually. JPM raises PT to $695 (Neutral), projecting 40% y/y FY27 growth. Stock fell 6-10% pre-market as Datacom disappointed HF expectations, but management signaled FY27 as another growth acceleration year. No China exposure flagged.

bullets.title: MU: UBS reiterates Buy, $1,625 PT; C2027 supply even tighter, HBM ASPs +79% Y/Y; <50% of DC requests fulfilled
bullets.body: UBS road-trip takeaways confirm C2027 supply-demand tighter than C2026 with MU fulfilling <50% of data-center customer volume requests. HBM ASPs expected to rise 79% Y/Y in C2027 as older contracts reprice; >50% of revenue under strategic customer agreements. DRAM capacity additions (ID1, Tongluo) online mid-C2027 with ~$75B projected cash by end of FQ1:27. PT unchanged at $1,625 on 11x C2029E EPS of ~$165.

bullets.title: PYPL: JPM recommends buying Jan27 $50 puts at $1.33; deal collapse could send stock to $47
bullets.body: JPM recommends purchasing PYPL Jan27 50 puts at $1.33, arguing the $60.50 takeout offer is viewed as insufficient and the acquirer is pivoting to a $7B OpenRouter deal instead. If the deal breaks, fast-money unwind could re-rate stock from 11x to ~8x forward EPS (~$47/sh). PYPL implied vol is at 1-year lows (0th percentile 5M ATM IV) with put/call ratio of 0.38, creating asymmetric spot-down/vol-up capture.

bullets.title: SNOW & INTU: UBS bullish on AI spend acceleration; INTU FY27 Online Ecosystem raised to +17.3%
bullets.body: UBS sees AI deployments driving faster Snowflake consumption with LLM displacement fears not materializing in enterprise budgets; maintains Buy. INTU FY27 Online Ecosystem revenue growth raised to 17.3% Y/Y (GBSG +12.9%) following earnings; pricing actions identified as incremental driver. INTU stock +1.5% pre-market following results.

bullets.title: META: Landmark $200B child addiction trial begins; 29 states seek platform overhaul
bullets.body: A federal bellwether trial opened today with 29 states suing Meta seeking up to $200B+ in penalties over allegations Facebook and Instagram were designed to addict young users. META disclosed the theoretical penalty framework could reach $1.4T; appeals expected to reduce exposure. Stock down ~1-3.5% pre-market. States demand removal of infinite scroll and recommendation systems; restrictions on young users also requested.

bullets.title: CRDO: GS TMT expects bullish AEC/optical guide; LITE/COHR/WDC/STX/MRVL down 5-6% pre-market
bullets.body: Credo expected to guide bullishly on FY2Q with AEC revenue and optical ramp visibility, per GS TMT. Broad memory/storage and optical complex under heavy pre-market pressure: LITE -6.1%, COHR -5.9%, MRVL -5.7%, STX -5.6%, WDC -5.6%, MU -4.2% on rising 30-year yields (5.32%, highest since 2007) and Anthropic ARR ($65B) coming in below the $80B+ whisper. VIAV seen positively by Rosenblatt: 1.6T test ASPs ~50% higher than 800G.

bullets.title: TSLA: Cybercab launches in Austin in August; Hedgeye maintains short on consumer/stagflation thesis
bullets.body: Tesla confirmed to staff it is gearing up for a public Cybercab launch in Austin as soon as this month, with employee rides first then robotaxi service. Hedgeye maintains a short on TSLA citing Quad 3 stagflation as a headwind for consumer discretionary; their risk range is buy $310 / sell $349 (bearish trend). Mizuho notes AV disruption for UBER is long-duration, not near-term earnings issue; Pony.ai and WeRide partnerships support UBER's multi-partner AV ecosystem.

bullets.title: NBIS: Vineland Phase 2 datacenter approved 9-1; 300MW facility supports $17.4B Microsoft contract
bullets.body: Vineland Planning Board voted 9-1 to approve Phase 2 of Nebius's AI infrastructure campus, removing a key land-use risk. The facility will be capable of 300MW to support the $17.4B Microsoft contract. Piper's analyst views approval as positive but prefers other AI-infra names at current levels. DA Davidson characterizes NBIS as avoiding regulatory challenges.

bullets.title: DIS/ABC: First Amendment lawsuit filed against FCC over station licensing probes
bullets.body: ABC filed a First Amendment lawsuit in Washington DC Federal Court against the FCC, claiming investigations into its 8 station licenses are part of a retaliatory campaign hindering free speech. The suit seeks to halt FCC proceedings demanding early renewal. Disney was expected to challenge FCC actions per prior reports.

bullets.title: FSLR: Morgan Stanley raises PT to $323 on Section 232 polysilicon tariff tailwinds; Overweight
bullets.body: MS raised FSLR price target from $245 to $323 following finalization of Section 232 polysilicon tariffs, which create a pricing floor on imports and improve barriers to entry. Analyst conservatively models realized average prices in upper $0.30/W range; 2030 EPS at $38.23 (ex-tax credits). Bull case raised to $474; analyst calls FSLR its favorite solar name. Stock currently at ~$220 with little credit priced for higher prices or bookings acceleration.

bullets.title: CRM: Citi reiterates Neutral ahead of Aug-26 earnings; vol skew bullish but checks mixed
bullets.body: Citi's field work showed modest improvement supporting 2H organic reacceleration with Agentforce positives, but Tableau/Marketing Cloud remain weak and customers are pushing for renewals discounting. Citi expects ~50bps beat on FX-adjusted cRPO; PT $204 (12.5x FY28 EV/FCF). Separately, Citi vol desk notes CRM realized vol at 86th percentile above implied (78th pct), with 1M 25-delta skew in 9th percentile—options positioning bullish despite stock down 28% YTD.

bullets.title: ADBE: Options positioning bullish with skew in 10th percentile; implied vol below realized
bullets.body: Citi vol strategy notes ADBE implied vol declined to 51.4 (84th pct), 2.6 pts below realized vol of 54 (98th pct); 1M 25-delta skew in 10th percentile, indicating options markets positioned bullishly into upcoming catalyst.

bullets.title: INTC: CEO Lip-Bu Tan buys $10M of stock, described as largest insider purchase in company history
bullets.body: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan purchased $10 million of INTC shares in a purchase described as the largest insider buy in the company's history, signaling management confidence in the turnaround.

bullets.title: BABA: Alipay AI commerce platform launch drives +3% pre-market; sells gaming unit for $2B+
bullets.body: Alibaba surged 3% pre-market on the launch of Alipay's all-in-one AI commerce merchant platform ahead of its August 20 earnings report. Alibaba also sold gaming studio Lingxi Games to Trustar Capital for $2B+, exiting in-house game development entirely to redirect proceeds toward AI infrastructure (original 380B yuan commitment already exceeded). JPM flags earnings as a key catalyst with HSTECH positioning near historical bottom.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Plans to exit all Pixel manufacturing from China by 2027; issues $5B AUD bond; $205B 2026 capex
bullets.body: Google has told suppliers all Pixel smartphones, watches, and earbuds will be manufactured outside China starting 2027 (shifting to Vietnam). Alphabet launched its first A$5B Australian-dollar bond sale across four maturities to fund up to $205B in 2026 capex for AI infrastructure. Google's TPUv9 development maintains dual-track inference/training strategy and is expected to take ~50% of TSMC N2 capacity.

bullets.title: APP: DIFF Eyewear scales to 10-15% of ad budget with META-par ROAS; holiday spend seen +20-30%
bullets.body: Jefferies expert call notes DIFF Eyewear scaled AppLovin to 10-15% of its total ad budget with ROAS on par with Meta, and expects holiday spend to increase 20-30% Y/Y on the platform. AppLovin founder also acknowledged past communications mistakes and radical product changes in a public interview.

bullets.title: AMZN: Hedgeye adding on dips ahead of Quad 1-2 re-acceleration; AWS flagged for $1T revenue path
bullets.body: Hedgeye flags AMZN approaching low-end of risk range as a buy-the-dip opportunity with Quad 1&2 entry points in Sep-Oct. Morgan Stanley highlights AWS's path to $1 trillion in revenue as a key growth theme. Druckenmiller's Duquesne significantly increased AMZN holdings in Q2. Hedgeye risk range: buy $258, sell $282 (bullish trend).

bullets.title: AXTI & LITE: InP supply thesis up 59% and 36% since Aug 2 call; test as key photonics bottleneck
bullets.body: Since the August 2 InP supply thesis call, AXTI is up ~59% (from $37 to $95) and LITE is up ~36%, tied to an unusually large prepayment deal between the two companies to secure long-term indium phosphide supply. LITE's CEO has emphasized InP criticality. Test is flagged as the next major bottleneck in photonics/optical manufacturing.

bullets.title: COHR: SiC substrate sampling begins; moving beyond optics into high-value thermal solutions
bullets.body: Coherent began customer sampling of 300mm high thermal conductivity silicon carbide substrates with up to 25% better heat spreading vs. current solutions, maintaining compatibility with existing components. One analyst notes COHR is at an inflection point moving beyond optical components into high-value thermal solutions for AI processors. Stock fell ~6% pre-market in the broad optical complex selloff.
